name: b-crosshatch-hospital-dusk
prompt: Vertical black-and-white editorial cartoon drawn with a steel nib in jet ink on cream pulp paper, every tone made by crosshatching, contour lines heavy and sure, no grey wash and not a speck of colour. Eye-level, straight-on view of a plain slatted park bench with scrolled iron legs, the bench and its two sitters occupying the bottom half. Seated on the left, a stout, pleased-with-himself plutocrat out of 1919, not a day older: stovepipe hat, a waistcoat straining across his paunch with a fob looped from its pocket, tailcoat, pinstriped trousers, pale spats, one knee over the other, nose in the air, lids drooping, his gloved hand flicked sideways to dismiss the woman beside him. Seated on the right, a worn-out young nurse in present-day scrubs, a lanyard and ID badge at her chest, bulky trainers, sagging into the slats with her eyes shut, a disposable coffee cup cradled in both hands on her lap. The park around them is contemporary but rendered with the same antique pen: a council litter bin at the bench's end, a sleek lamp post with a USB charging point, leafless trees, and rising behind the branches a big hospital block hatched almost solid black, its lit windows reserved as rows of tiny bare-paper rectangles. Dusk light glows faintly from behind the hospital, so hatching grows denser toward the ground and the building's base. The upper quarter is open, nearly untouched sky with only a few faint strokes, kept empty for a caption. Ink only; no letters, words, signature or dialogue bubbles.
